When making a left turn you must yield the right-of-way to oncoming traffic.

You must yield to any ambulance, fire or police vehicle sounding a siren and flashing warning lights by pulling to the right edge of the road clear of the intersection and stopping until it has passed, keeping your foot on the brake so the emergency driver knows you are stopped, and watching for other emergency vehicles before proceeding.

Passing is prohibited within one hundred feet of a bridge, viaduct, tunnel or underpass and within one hundred feet of any railroad crossing.

Passing is also prohibited when an approaching vehicle is within your passing area, when a sign or highway marking tells you to keep right or not to overtake, when the vehicle ahead has stopped at an intersection to let a pedestrian cross, and when the solid yellow line is in your lane.
The one-hundred-foot no-passing buffer applies before a bridge, viaduct, tunnel, underpass and any railroad crossing, while a solid yellow line in your lane bans passing at any distance.

why_how.text: Before passing on a two-lane highway make sure you are in a passing zone and keeping the three-to-four second following distance, and decide whether passing is necessary, because if you have to speed to pass you probably do not need to pass.

Check ahead, to the rear and to the side before starting to pass, look for other dangers in the passing area such as a narrow bridge, side road or curve, and signal early enough that other drivers know your intentions.
Move left when the way is clear and sound your horn to alert the driver ahead that you are passing, and at night you may also blink your headlights to signal that you are about to pass.

Signal and return to your lane when you can see the front of the passed vehicle, both headlights, in your rear view mirror, and passing on the right is not permissible unless there is a lane designated for passing.
You cannot pass safely unless you can see far enough ahead, you can return to your lane before meeting oncoming traffic, and your vehicle is capable of the speed needed to pass.
Passing is done on the left, and passing on the right is allowed only where a lane is designated for passing.
The horn alerts the driver ahead that you are passing by day, and at night a blink of the headlights may serve the same purpose.
You return to your lane only when both headlights of the passed vehicle show in your rear view mirror, not when its front bumper merely drops behind you.
